newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's Mazeedi to sign Tunisia pipeline deal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's Mazeedi to sign Tunisia pipeline deal.

text.p: Kuwaiti Oil Minister Isa al-Mazeedi will sign a deal with Tunisia to build an oil pipeline in the North African state, the Kuwait News Agency said on Wednesday.
The pipeline would link Sidi Kilani oilfield, which is partly owned by the state-owned Kuwait Foreign Petroleum Exploration Co (KUFPEC), with La Skhira port, said the official Kuwait News Agency.
It did not give further details about the deal which it said would be signed during a three-day visit to Tunisia by Mazeedi that he started on Wednesday.
Mazeedi will also discuss means of cooperation between the two Arab states.

KUFPEC owns 45 percent of the Sidi Kilani oilfield whose production is estimated at about 17,000 barrels per day, industry sources said. Tunisia's Enterprise Tunisienne d'Activites Petrolieres (ETAP) owns 55 percent of the field.
Currently crude is carried by road tankers to a pipelne at Sidi el Itayem pumping station where it is transfered by pipeline to the southern oil port of La Skhira.
Sidi Kilani is some 190 km (120 mile) south of Tunis.

Mazeedi will also visit Dallas to meet officials from Santa Fe International, which was fully-owned by Kuwait until it sold about 35 percent of its shares earlier this year, the agency said without elaboration.
